case_name: Emerging (pre-adoption) allocation with identified planning activity
commercial_scenario: A rare combination in the current universe (only 2 of 229 strategic-land candidates): identified planning activity despite the LOCAL PLAN itself still being emerging/pre-adoption. Tests whether the model over-weights activity against plan immaturity or reasons about the two dimensions independently.

- target_unit_max [TARGET]: A scheme above 300 total homes is a soft/contextual signal, worth investigating (e.g. for a suitable phase/parcel), never a disqualifying fact on its own - no current mandate has a hard maximum, and this module does not add one.
- accepted_planning_states [PREFERENCE  (active)]: A planning state outside this set is a soft signal (unknown/context), never a disqualifying fact on its own.
- specialist_development_is_exclusion [EXCLUSION  (active)]: A confirmed specialist development is a hard exclusion for this buyer.
- wholly_affordable_is_exclusion [EXCLUSION  (active)]: A confirmed wholly-affordable scheme is a hard exclusion for this buyer.
- treats_no_activity_as_positive [PREFERENCE  (active)]: No identified planning activity on a strategic land allocation reads as a positive signal for this buyer.

- large_allocation_is_self_qualifying [TOLERANCE  (active)]: An oversized strategic land allocation is read as a meaningful position in its own right for this buyer, independent of a confirmed smaller parcel.
- geography_scope [HARD_CONSTRAINT]: This buyer has not stated a geographic boundary that excludes anything.
- development_state_appetite [PREFERENCE  (active)]: This buyer's stated development-state appetite is 'UNCOMMENCED_PREFERRED' - a leaning, never an exclusion.

commercial_rationale: HELD - Product Owner instructed a read-only investigation of what has_identified_planning_activity=True actually represents before any expected_recommendation is approved (Case Correction Gate, Section 5). Not yet approved to any label.
reviewer_notes: READ-ONLY INVESTIGATION FINDING (2026-09-15): RELATIONSHIP NOT DETERMINED. The allocation (site 170, Wigan) is the 'North Leigh Park' scheme: a 2012 outline consent for 1,800 homes (app A/12/76665, decided/approved, applicant/developer 'North Leigh Park Group Limited'), substantially implemented since 2019 via reserved-matters/condition-discharge applications naming 'Countryside Properties (UK) Limited' as developer (confirmed CONFIRMED_PHASED phasing evidence: 'Phase 1a(1)', 'Phase 1b', 'future phases' - first phase lawfully implemented 2 Dec 2019), PLUS a newly REGISTERED (undecided) 1,491-unit reserved-matters application from 'Vistry Group' (A/26/100520/RMMAJ) on the same site. Despite this, the platform's own deterministic per-Site development-coverage accounting (app.reporting.allocation_development_coverage.build_allocation_development_coverage) currently returns identified_application_capacity=2 for this site - an evident data-quality artifact in representative-application selection, not a true reflection of the real, well-documented activity. Separately and more fundamentally: NONE of this coverage percentage, phasing classification, or linked-applicant/developer detail is exposed to the Agent Evaluation Policy V1 evaluator at all for a strategic_land opportunity - build_prompt_context() only ever renders the bare has_identified_planning_activity boolean. The model cannot currently distinguish 'no activity' from 'a well-documented, 1,800+1,491-home multi-phase scheme is already progressing on this allocation' - this is an architecture-boundary gap, not something the benchmark case alone can paper over. Recommend: do not approve any expected_recommendation for this case until either (a) a different, cleaner seed identity is substituted, or (b) Agent Evaluation Policy V1's own evidence layer is extended to surface allocation-development-coverage detail for strategic_land opportunities (a separate, larger change outside benchmark scope).
